title: Year 6 Multiplying and Dividing Fractions
seo_title: Year 6 Multiplying and Dividing Fractions Worksheets: Fraction × Fraction, Fraction ÷ Whole Number, Simplest Form (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Multiply simple pairs of proper fractions, writing the answer in its simplest form [for example, 1/4 × 1/2 = 1/8]; divide proper fractions by whole numbers [for example, 1/3 ÷ 2 = 1/6].
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on multiplying and dividing fractions for the National Curriculum: fractions of amounts, area models, fraction × fraction in simplest form, fraction ÷ whole number and SATs-style word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Fraction × fraction: multiply the numerators, multiply the denominators, then simplify. Fraction ÷ whole number: share it into equal parts.
body_html:
The big idea

When you multiply by a fraction, × means “of”. 14 × 12 means a quarter of a half. When you divide a fraction by a whole number, you share it into equal parts. 13 ÷ 2 means half of a third.

Fraction × whole number

Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator.

Example

23 × 5 = ?

Multiply the whole number by the numerator: 5 × 2 = 10, so the answer is 103. 10 ÷ 3 = 3 remainder 1.

Answer: 3 13

Fraction × fraction

Multiply the numerators. Multiply the denominators. Then simplify. The area model shows why: the square is cut into (denominator × denominator) equal parts.

Example

23 × 34 = ?

2 × 3 = 6 and 3 × 4 = 12, so the answer is 612. Divide the numerator and denominator by 6.

Answer: 12

Tip: you can simplify before you multiply. In 34 × 29, divide 3 and 9 by 3, and 2 and 4 by 2: 12 × 13 = 16.

Fraction ÷ whole number

Dividing by 2 is the same as finding half, or multiplying by 12.

MethodExampleWhen to use it
Divide the numerator45 ÷ 2 = 25The numerator divides exactly
Multiply the denominator25 ÷ 3 = 215Any time
Example

23 ÷ 4 = ?

4 does not go into 2 exactly, so multiply the denominator: 3 × 4 = 12. 23 ÷ 4 = 212. Simplify by dividing by 2.

Answer: 16

Check by multiplying back: 16 × 4 = 46 = 23.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
14 × 12 = 26 (adding numerators and denominators)Multiply: 1 × 1 = 1 and 4 × 2 = 8, so 18
13 ÷ 2 = 23 (multiplying by 2)Dividing makes the part smaller: 16
45 ÷ 2 = 810 (multiplying the numerator and denominator)810 = 45, so nothing changed. The answer is 25
35 × 20 = 60100 (multiplying the numerator and denominator by 20)Only multiply the numerator: 605 = 12

faq.q: How do you multiply fractions in Year 6?
faq.a: Multiply the numerators, multiply the denominators, then simplify. For example, 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2.

faq.q: How do you divide a fraction by a whole number?
faq.a: If the numerator divides exactly, divide it: 4/5 ÷ 2 = 2/5. Otherwise multiply the denominator by the whole number: 1/3 ÷ 2 = 1/6.

faq.q: Do Year 6 pupils divide a fraction by a fraction?
faq.a: No. In the National Curriculum, Year 6 divides proper fractions by whole numbers only. Dividing by a fraction comes in Key Stage 3.

faq.q: Are multiplying and dividing fractions in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: Yes. The arithmetic paper (Paper 1) usually includes calculations such as 3/4 × 1/6 or 2/5 ÷ 4, and the reasoning papers use fractions in word problems.

sets.title: Fraction × whole number and fractions of amounts

items.q: The whole bar is 20. What is 35 × 20?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 4 = 12. So 35 of 20 = 12. (Do not multiply the denominator by 20 as well: 60100 is just 35.)

items.q: The whole bar is 24. What is 34 × 24?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 6 = 18. So 34 of 24 = 18.

items.q: The whole bar is 18. What is 23 × 18?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 6 = 12. So 23 of 18 = 12.

items.q: The whole bar is 40. What is 58 × 40?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 40 ÷ 8 = 5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 5 × 5 = 25. So 58 of 40 = 25.

items.q: The whole bar is 28. What is 47 × 28?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 28 ÷ 7 = 4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 4 × 4 = 16. So 47 of 28 = 16.

items.q: 38 × 24 = ?
items.e: × means “of”. Divide by the denominator: 24 ÷ 8 = 3 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 3 = 9. So 38 of 24 = 9.

items.q: 36 × 34 = ?
items.e: × means “of”. Divide by the denominator: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 9 = 27. So 34 of 36 = 27.

items.q: Find 56 of 30.
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 30 ÷ 6 = 5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 5 × 5 = 25. So 56 of 30 = 25.

items.q: 710 × 50 = ?
items.e: × means “of”. Divide by the denominator: 50 ÷ 10 = 5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 7 × 5 = 35. So 710 of 50 = 35.

items.q: Find 29 of 45.
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 45 ÷ 9 = 5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 5 = 10. So 29 of 45 = 10.

items.q: 48 × 512 = ?
items.e: × means “of”. Divide by the denominator: 48 ÷ 12 = 4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 5 × 4 = 20. So 512 of 48 = 20.

items.q: Find 35 of 35.
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 7 = 21. So 35 of 35 = 21.

items.q:
23 × 5 = ?
Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Multiply the whole number by the numerator and keep the denominator: 5 × 2 = 10, so the answer is 103. 10 ÷ 3 = 3 remainder 1, so it is 3 13.

items.q:

Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Multiply the whole number by the numerator and keep the denominator: 6 × 3 = 18, so the answer is 184. Simplify: 184 = 92. 9 ÷ 2 = 4 remainder 1, so it is 4 12.

items.q:

items.e: Multiply the whole number by the numerator and keep the denominator: 5 × 3 = 15, so the answer is 158. 15 ÷ 8 = 1 remainder 7, so it is 1 78.

items.q:

Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Multiply the whole number by the numerator and keep the denominator: 7 × 4 = 28, so the answer is 285. 28 ÷ 5 = 5 remainder 3, so it is 5 35.

Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: Multiply the whole number by the numerator and keep the denominator: 7 × 5 = 35, so the answer is 356. 35 ÷ 6 = 5 remainder 5, so it is 5 56.

items.q: Which is greater: 34 of 20 or 23 of 24?
items.e: 34 of 20: 20 ÷ 4 = 5, 5 × 3 = 15. 23 of 24: 24 ÷ 3 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16. 16 is greater than 15, so 23 of 24 is greater.

items.q: 3? of 40 = 15. What is the missing denominator?
items.e: 15 is 3 parts, so 1 part is 15 ÷ 3 = 5. 40 ÷ 5 = 8, so 40 is split into 8 equal parts: 38 of 40 = 15. The missing denominator is 8.

items.q: 25 of a number is 14. What is the number?
items.e: 2 parts are 14, so 1 part is 14 ÷ 2 = 7. The whole has 5 parts: 7 × 5 = 35. Check: 25 of 35 = 35 ÷ 5 × 2 = 14.

sets.title: Divide a fraction by a whole number

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 13. It is split into 2 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
13 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: Follow the dashed lines: the whole bar is cut into 3 × 2 = 6 equal parts, and the dark part is 1 of them. Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by 12. Multiply the denominator by 2: 13 ÷ 2 = 16. Check: 16 × 2 = 26 = 13.

items.e: Follow the dashed lines: the whole bar is cut into 2 × 4 = 8 equal parts, and the dark part is 1 of them. Dividing by 4 is the same as multiplying by 14. Multiply the denominator by 4: 12 ÷ 4 = 18. Check: 18 × 4 = 48 = 12.

items.q: Lily says 13 ÷ 2 = 23. What did she do?
c: She multiplied the numerator and the denominator by 2.
She multiplied by 2 instead of dividing.
items.e: Lily found 13 × 2 = 23. Dividing must give a smaller answer. Splitting 13 into 2 equal parts gives 16 each: 13 ÷ 2 = 16.

items.q: Alfie says 45 ÷ 2 = 810. What did he do?
c: He multiplied the numerator and the denominator by 2.
He multiplied by 2 instead of dividing.
items.e: 810 = 45, so Alfie did not change the size at all. Divide the numerator instead: 4 ÷ 2 = 2, so 45 ÷ 2 = 25.

items.q: 34 × 16 = ?

items.q: 56 ÷ 5 = ?

items.q: 25 × 35 = ?
items.e: × means “of”. Divide by the denominator: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 7 = 14. So 25 of 35 = 14.

items.q: 78 ÷ 2 = ?

items.q: 34 of a pizza is left. Amelia eats half of what is left. What fraction of the whole pizza does she eat?
items.e: Half of 34 means 12 × 34. Multiply the numerators: 1 × 3 = 3. Multiply the denominators: 2 × 4 = 8. So 12 × 34 = 38. This is already in its simplest form: 38. She eats 38 of the pizza.

items.q: 23 of a cake is left. Mohammed shares it equally between 4 friends. What fraction of the whole cake does each friend get?
items.e: Share 23 between 4: 23 ÷ 4. Dividing by 4 is the same as multiplying by 14. Multiply the denominator by 4: 23 ÷ 4 = 212. Simplify: 212 = 16. Check: 16 × 4 = 46 = 23.

items.q: A bottle holds 34 of a litre of juice. It is poured equally into 3 glasses. How much juice is in each glass?
items.e: 34 ÷ 3: The numerator 3 can be divided by 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1. Keep the denominator: 34 ÷ 3 = 14 litre. Check: 14 × 3 = 34.

items.q: Aisha has a ribbon 25 m long. She cuts it into 2 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 25 ÷ 2: The numerator 2 can be divided by 2: 2 ÷ 2 = 1. Keep the denominator: 25 ÷ 2 = 15 m. Check: 15 × 2 = 25.

items.q: There are 30 pupils in a Year 6 class. 35 of them walk to school. How many pupils walk to school?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 6 = 18. So 35 of 30 = 18.

items.q: A pair of trainers costs £40. In a sale, Harry pays 58 of the price. How much does he pay?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: £40 ÷ 8 = £5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 5 × £5 = £25. So 58 of £40 = £25.

items.q: 23 of a garden is lawn. 14 of the lawn has daisies on it. What fraction of the whole garden has daisies?
items.e: 14 of 23 means 14 × 23. Multiply the numerators: 1 × 2 = 2. Multiply the denominators: 4 × 3 = 12. So 14 × 23 = 212. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator by 2: 212 = 16.

items.q: 45 kg of flour is shared equally between 4 bags. How much flour is in each bag?
items.e: 45 ÷ 4: The numerator 4 can be divided by 4: 4 ÷ 4 = 1. Keep the denominator: 45 ÷ 4 = 15 kg. Check: 15 × 4 = 45.

items.q: 12 of the pupils in a school have school dinners. 13 of these pupils choose pasta. What fraction of all the pupils choose pasta?
items.e: 13 of 12 means 13 × 12. Multiply the numerators: 1 × 1 = 1. Multiply the denominators: 3 × 2 = 6. So 13 × 12 = 16. This is already in its simplest form: 16.

items.q: One lap of the school field is 38 km. Maya runs 4 laps. How far does she run?
items.e: 38 × 4 = 128. Simplify: 128 = 32. 3 ÷ 2 = 1 remainder 1, so she runs 1 12 km.

items.q: A plank of wood is 56 m long. It is cut into 5 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 56 ÷ 5: The numerator 5 can be divided by 5: 5 ÷ 5 = 1. Keep the denominator: 56 ÷ 5 = 16 m. Check: 16 × 5 = 56.

items.q: Poppy has £15 of pocket money. She spends 25 of it on a book. How much does the book cost?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: £15 ÷ 5 = £3 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × £3 = £6. So 25 of £15 = £6.

items.q: A rectangle is 34 m long and 25 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 34 × 25 = 620. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator by 2: 310 m².

items.q: Ethan eats 12 of 14 of a pie. Ruby eats 13 of 13 of a pie the same size. Who eats more pie?
items.e: Ethan: 12 × 14 = 18. Ruby: 13 × 13 = 19. Both have a numerator of 1, and eighths are bigger than ninths, so 18 is more than 19. Ethan eats more pie.

items.q: A 1 litre jug is 56 full of squash. Charlie pours it equally into 2 cups. How much squash is in each cup?
items.e: 56 ÷ 2: Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by 12. Multiply the denominator by 2: 56 ÷ 2 = 512 litre. Check: 512 × 2 = 1012 = 56.
